metadata.title: Multigraph Sampling of Online Social Networks

extraction_notes.note: The prose description of the two-stage neighbor selection just before Algorithm 1 ('First, we select... Second, we pick...') restates the pseudocode, so it got no separate node; the equivalence sentence after it is ClP2.

Most of Sections 3-4 are experimental results read off figures and tables (Gelman-Rubin plots, isolate percentages, weekly charts); only a few headline empirical claims were emitted, as numerical-rigor claims.
remark or external theorem: the cited link between lambda_2 and mixing time is stated only qualitatively, so it is kept as an external remark.
remark or claim plus external theorem: the paragraph computes p*, cites the ER connectivity threshold and concludes intuitively in one go, so it is one remark rather than separate nodes.

The \label{alg:mixture} sits after \end{algorithmic}, so the finishing step did not tie it to the algorithm node; the uses edges from AP3 for each \ref{alg:mixture} were added by hand at confidence 0.9.
The algorithm steps of these prose procedures are sub-sentence spans (one operation each) inside a single sentence.

nodes.statement: Let d(v,u)=d(u,v) be the number of edges between nodes v and u in the union multigraph G. The sampling process of Algorithm~ is a Markov chain on V with transition probabilities P_vu=fracd(v,u)d(v), u,v in V. So long as G is finite and connected, this random walk is irreducible and positive recurrent. The presence of a triangle within G further guarantees aperiodicity. A Markov chain of this type is equivalent to a random walk on an undirected weighted graph with edge weights w(v,u)=d(v,u). A random walk on weighted graph is known to have the unique equilibrium distribution pi(v)=fracw(v)sum_uin V w(u), where w(v)=sum_u w(v,u) (e.g., see ), and the proof follows immediately by substitution.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $d(v,u)=d(u,v)$ be the number of edges between nodes $v$ and $u$ in the union multigraph $G$.
The sampling process of Algorithm~\ref{alg:mixture} is a Markov chain on $V$ with transition probabilities $P_{vu}=\frac{d(v,u)}{d(v)}, u,v \in V$.  So long as $G$ is finite and connected,
this random walk is irreducible and positive recurrent. The presence of a triangle within $G$ further guarantees aperiodicity.








A Markov chain of this type is equivalent to a random walk on an undirected weighted graph with edge weights $w(v,u)=d(v,u)$.
A random walk on weighted graph is known to have the unique equilibrium distribution
$\pi(v)=\frac{w(v)}{\sum_{u\in V} w(u)}$, where  $w(v)=\sum_{u} w(v,u)$
({\em e.g., } see \cite[Example 4.32]{RossBook}), and the proof follows immediately by substitution.
